speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome. I see you have sudden onset abdominal pain; can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is it?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your recent myocardial infarction and bloody stools, have you experienced any chest pain, shortness of breath, or lightheadedness since the MI? Also, has anyone noticed a pulsating mass in your abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm with rupture and mesenteric ischemia.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound, CT_Angiography_Abdomen_Pelvis.
